title: El chavalo
goal: Be asked for money by a kid, and work out what you think
culture: Handing cash to a child is complicated here — it can keep him out of school and there is often somebody older collecting it. Buying him something to eat is unambiguous, ordinary, and nobody will look at you twice for doing it. He gets VOS, because he is a child, and getting that right matters more than the money does.

beats.es: Regáleme diez pesos, chele. Para comer.
beats.objective: Say you have not got it
beats.good: The plain truth, said to him rather than past him. Chavalo on the end is friendly — it is what everybody calls him.

beats.objective: Offer to buy him food instead
beats.en: I’ll buy you something to eat.
beats.good: TE compro — vos, because he is a child. Food instead of cash is the ordinary thing to do here and nobody will think it mean.

beats.objective: Ask whether he has eaten today
beats.good: ¿Comiste? is spelled the same in vos and in tú, which is why it slips past learners. Asking is not charity; it is what any adult here would ask him.
Andá, not vaya. He is nine and he gets vos — cuídese to a child would be as odd as calling him sir.
